summary: This 2013 Nissan Altima is priced at $4,500, which is below market value, but it has a high record of transmission and airbag issues. You must confirm that all safety recalls were completed and have a mechanic check the transmission before buying.

recalls.summary_plain: A replacement seat sensor might incorrectly think the front passenger seat is empty.
recalls.remedy_plain: Nissan dealers will update the seat sensor software for free.

recalls.summary_plain: An incorrect control unit may misclassify the front passenger.
recalls.remedy_plain: Dealers will replace the control unit and update software for free.

recalls.summary_plain: A loose seal where the fuel line meets the tank can leak gas during a crash.
recalls.remedy_plain: Dealers will install a locking ring on the fuel tank for free.

recalls.summary_plain: Passenger seat software may falsely detect an adult seat as empty.
recalls.remedy_plain: Dealers will update the air bag software free of charge.

recalls.summary_plain: The passenger seat sensor may mistake an adult for a child and turn off the air bag.
recalls.remedy_plain: Dealers will reprogram or replace the air bag control units for free.

recalls.summary_plain: The backup hood latch can stick open, letting the hood fly up while driving.
recalls.remedy_plain: Dealers will replace the hood latch with a new one for free.

recalls.summary_plain: Rust and debris can cause the backup hood latch to stick open.
recalls.remedy_plain: Dealers will adjust, clean, or replace the hood latch mechanism for free.

recalls.summary_plain: An expanded recall for hood latches sticking in the unlatched position.
recalls.remedy_plain: Dealers will modify or replace the latch assembly for free.

recalls.summary_plain: Sensors in the passenger seat were built incorrectly and may shut off the air bag.
recalls.remedy_plain: Dealers will inspect and replace the seat sensors for free.

recalls.summary_plain: The spare tire inside the trunk may have too much or too little air from the factory.
recalls.remedy_plain: Dealers will check and set the spare tire pressure for free.

recalls.summary_plain: Steering and suspension bolts were not tightened properly at the factory and could fall out.
recalls.remedy_plain: Dealers will tighten the bolts to the proper specs for free.

recalls.summary_plain: The secondary hood latch lever can rust and jam over time.
recalls.remedy_plain: Dealers will install a stronger spring and provide maintenance instructions for free.

known_problems.explanation: The continuous transmission (the system sending power to wheels) frequently hesitates, shudders, or fails early.
Passenger seat sensors often fail to detect adults, disabling safety air bags.
Low-beam headlights lose brightness over time due to inner lens degradation.
Struts and shocks (parts that cushion bumps) tend to wear out around this mileage, causing clunking noises.
Miscellaneous complaints cover interior trim, door latches, and accessory electronics.
Engine mounts wear down, creating shaking or vibration when idling.

maintenance_due.why: Worn spark plugs cause engine misfires and poor fuel mileage.
Fresh fluid protects the sensitive automatic transmission from early failure.
Brake fluid absorbs moisture over time, reducing stopping power.
Clean filters keep dirt out of the engine and keep cabin air fresh.

declined_services.risk_if_ignored: Ignoring fluid changes can cause total transmission failure, leaving the car unable to move.
Old plugs can damage ignition coils and reduce engine power.
Moisture in the brake lines can rust internal parts and cause a soft brake pedal.

diy_cards.job: Engine Air Filter and Cabin Filter Replacement

diy_cards.safety_note: Ensure the engine is completely cool before removing spark plugs.
Brakes are critical for safety. Have a professional check the work if you are unsure.

inspect: Test drive for any transmission slipping, shaking, or slow response when accelerating
Check that the low-beam headlights are bright enough at night
Listen for knocking noises from the suspension when driving over bumps
Check the hood latch mechanism for rust or sticking
should_be_done: Hire an independent mechanic to do a full Pre-Purchase Inspection (PPI)
Run the VIN through a Nissan dealer to confirm all 12 recall repairs were completed
ask_seller: Do you have service records showing regular CVT transmission fluid changes?
Has the hood latch recall fix been completed by a Nissan dealer?
Why is the asking price lower than typical market value?

disclaimers: Costs and difficulty are estimates, not quotes.
Brakes, airbags, and fuel lines: have a professional check your work.
